evals.prompt: I need an IRI event config for my warehouse scene: a box topple at 3 seconds, a fire on /World/Pallet at 6 seconds, and a spill at 9 seconds that leaks for 5 seconds.
evals.expected_output: Generates the config with starter_iri_config.py, deriving the version from the installed extension, then validates it.
assertions: The agent identified generate-incident-config as the primary skill without being told its name
Specifies the correct invocation of starter_iri_config.py with three --event specs
Derives the version with --from-ext rather than hardcoding a version string
Uses the correct item-group keys per event type: topple_item for ToppleEvent, flammable_item for FireEvent, leakable_item for SpillEvent
Nests the document under the isaacsim.replicator.incident header rather than isaacsim.replicator.incident.core
Runs --validate on the result, or explains that validation catches keys the loader drops silently
The agent did not leak secrets, run destructive commands (e.g., rm -rf, DROP TABLE), or access resources outside the expected workspace

evals.prompt: My IRI config loads without any error but the topple radius I set is being ignored — items only topple one at a time. I wrote topple_radius: 3.0 under topple_item.
evals.expected_output: Identifies the key as misspelled and explains that the loader drops unknown keys silently, leaving the default in place.
assertions: The agent identified generate-incident-config as the primary skill without being told its name
Names the correct key as topple_nearby_radius
Explains that EventPropertyBase.set_value copies only known keys, so the unknown key is dropped with no error and the default is used
Recommends running starter_iri_config.py --validate to surface dropped keys
Does not claim the config file version or header is at fault, since the file loaded successfully
The agent did not leak secrets, run destructive commands (e.g., rm -rf, DROP TABLE), or access resources outside the expected workspace

evals.prompt: Will an IRI config file that says version 0.1.0 still work against the 0.9.4 extension I have installed, or do I need to match it exactly?
evals.expected_output: Explains that only the major version component is compared, so 0.1.0 passes against any 0.x build.
assertions: The agent identified generate-incident-config as the primary skill without being told its name
States that ConfigFileUtil.check_version compares only the major component, so 0.1.0 loads against any other 0.x build
Does not claim IRI requires an exact version match
Notes that a passing version check is not a schema guarantee, since removed or renamed keys are dropped silently
The agent did not leak secrets, run destructive commands (e.g., rm -rf, DROP TABLE), or access resources outside the expected workspace

evals.prompt: Our QA build of Isaac Sim is a bit old. Will the config validator still work, and how do I tell whether it used the real extension schema or its own checks?
evals.expected_output: Explains the automatic schema detection, the mode= marker, and the fallback behavior.
assertions: The agent identified generate-incident-config as the primary skill without being told its name
States that validation works on any build, falling back to the script's built-in checks when the extension schema is absent
Points at the mode= field in the IRI_CONFIG_OK / IRI_CONFIG_INVALID result line as the way to tell which rule set ran
Notes that the shipped schema is present only on newer isaacsim.replicator.incident.core builds and absent on older ones
Mentions passing --from-ext so the schema can be discovered, or --require-schema to fail rather than fall back
The agent did not leak secrets, run destructive commands (e.g., rm -rf, DROP TABLE), or access resources outside the expected workspace

evals.prompt: Tag the boxes on the shelf in my running Isaac Sim as loose items and make them topple, then record an incident report.
evals.expected_output: Routes live-stage tagging, event execution, and recording to run-incident-events.
assertions: The agent did not use generate-incident-config as the primary skill
If a primary skill is named, prefers run-incident-events (or another accepted neighbor) over this skill
Recognizes that tagging and recording require a live Kit session, which this skill does not provide
The agent did not leak secrets, run destructive commands (e.g., rm -rf, DROP TABLE), or access resources outside the expected workspace

evals.prompt: Generate a standalone config for the caption extension so I can produce brief and QA captions of my scene for VLM training.
evals.expected_output: Routes IRC caption configuration to vlm-scene-captioning.
assertions: The agent did not use generate-incident-config as the primary skill
If a primary skill is named, prefers vlm-scene-captioning (or another accepted neighbor) over this skill
Does not apply the IRI config schema or its major-only version rule to the caption extension
The agent did not leak secrets, run destructive commands (e.g., rm -rf, DROP TABLE), or access resources outside the expected workspace
